package_info.package_name: Popup Builder WordPress plugin (malicious Custom JS injection)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all vulnerable versions with stored XSS flaw)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers exploit a stored XSS vulnerability in the Popup Builder plugin to inject malicious JavaScript into the Custom JS or CSS sections, resulting in unauthorized redirections and malware delivery to site visitors.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits an infected site page)
execution_context.file_location: Popup Builder plugin's Custom JS section (stored in WordPress database, rendered in page HTML)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes in the browser of any visitor to an infected site, reads the user's cookies, and redirects the browser to a malicious domain, enabling credential theft or further malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code performs an unsolicited redirect to an external domain and exfiltrates user cookies, which is a classic sign of malicious XSS activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Custom JS in a WordPress plugin should enhance site functionality, not steal user data or redirect users to malicious sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate redirects may occur for login flows or A/B testing, but never with user cookies appended to third-party domains.
key_indicators: Direct use of document.cookie in client-side code
Unsolicited window.location assignment to external domain
Presence of script tags in Custom JS/CSS fields

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits stored XSS vulnerability in Popup Builder plugin to inject malicious JavaScript into the Custom JS section.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is stored in the WordPress database and rendered on site pages.

attack_chain.action: When a user visits an infected page, the malicious JavaScript executes in their browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected to a malicious domain, and their cookies may be exfiltrated.

attack_chain.action: Malicious domain may deliver further malware or steal user credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: credential theft, malware infection, or further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of <script> tags in Custom JS/CSS fields of WordPress plugins
Client-side code that reads document.cookie and sends it to external domains
file_indicators: Custom JS/CSS fields in Popup Builder plugin containing <script> tags
Unexpected modifications to wp_options or plugin-specific database tables
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the legitimate site
Redirections to known malicious or newly registered domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the contents of Custom JS/CSS fields in WordPress plugins for script tags or suspicious JavaScript. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to block or alert on outbound requests containing user cookies or unsolicited redirects. Regularly scan site pages for injected scripts and monitor for unexpected changes in plugin configuration or database entries.
